payload.stem: Which of the following is the weakest precondition (the least restrictive condition) that guarantees the method will not throw an exception?

options.text: Neither first nor last is the empty string.
options.why: When this condition is false substring asks for characters that are not there and throws a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException; when it is true every call works.

options.text: first and last contain only letters.
options.why: The characters are never examined, only the positions, so the kind of character does not matter.

options.text: Only first is not the empty string.
options.why: A call such as initials("Ana", "") still throws an exception because last has no character at index 0.

options.text: Both first and last have at least two characters.
options.why: This is stronger than needed: one character in each String already works, so it is not the weakest condition.

payload.stem: Which of the following best describes the postcondition of the method steps (what is true about the returned value when the method finishes)?

options.text: It returns n minus 3, the value of n after one subtraction of 3.
options.why: The loop keeps subtracting while at least 3 remain, and the method returns the count rather than the value of n.

options.text: It returns the remainder of n divided by 3, the value left in n when the loop ends.
options.why: The loop counts subtractions in c and returns c; the remainder is the final value of n, which is not returned.

options.text: It returns the number of digits that are needed to write n in base 3.
options.why: The loop does not divide repeatedly; it subtracts a fixed amount once per pass, which is not a digit count.
